mainTopic: Can a married woman's sale or gift of her נכסי מלוג hold up against her husband after she dies? A real case involving רב שמואל בר אבא, and רבי ירמיה בר אבא's proof from a משנה about a father who writes his property to his son.
overview: רב שמואל בר אבא claims property his mother wrote over to him, and רבי ירמיה בר אבא rules that it is his. Her husband, רבי אבא, brings the case to רב יהודה. רב יהודה quotes שמואל: if a wife sells her נכסי מלוג and then dies, the husband takes the property back. רבי ירמיה answers with a משנה about a father who writes his property to his son 'after death.' He reads it the way ריש לקיש does, against רבי יוחנן, to show that קנין פירות is not like קנין הגוף, so the mother's transfer should hold. רב יהודה replies in the name of שמואל that the wife's case is not like that משנה. רב יוסף explains the difference as the son being an heir, but אביי rejects that explanation. אביי says the real reason is the תקנת אושא, a special rabbinic rule that lets a husband take back his wife's sold נכסי מלוג. רב אידי בר אבין then begins quoting a teaching about divorce witnesses to support the תקנת אושא, and the proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה gives the property to the son
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר אבא comes before רבי ירמיה בר אבא to claim his mother's property, and רבי ירמיה rules that it is his.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר אבא went before רבי ירמיה בר אבא, and רבי ירמיה established him as owner of the property.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a real court case. רבי ירמיה בר אבא rules that the property written to רב שמואל בר אבא belongs to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mother had written her property over to her son, and the question is whether that transfer holds up after she dies. רבי ירמיה says it does, so the son gets the property. This ruling is what the rest of the passage will test.

keyTerms.meaning: before him, in front of him
he established him, put him in possession

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Abba went
before Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba,
he established him in the property.
phrases.notes: רבי ירמיה ruled the property belongs to the son and let him take it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲזַל רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַבָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the mother's property begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The son is given ownership of the property his mother wrote to him.

steps.title: שמואל rules that the husband takes the property back
steps.stepSummary: The husband, רבי אבא, takes the case to רב הושעיא, who takes it to רב יהודה. רב יהודה quotes שמואל: a wife's sale of נכסי מלוג does not hold against her husband once she dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא went and told the matter to רב הושעיא, and רב הושעיא told it to רב יהודה. רב יהודה said: This is what שמואל said: If a woman sold her נכסי מלוג while her husband was alive, and then she died, the husband takes it back from the buyers.
steps.whatsHappening: The husband takes the case up the chain of rabbis. רב יהודה answers with a ruling of שמואל that goes against what רבי ירמיה decided.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נכסי מלוג belong to the wife, but the husband eats their profits. שמואל says that if she sells them and then dies, the sale fails and the husband takes them back. Her writing the property over to her son is treated like a sale, so רבי ירמיה's ruling looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: a wife's own property whose profits go to her husband
takes it back from the buyers

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the names: רבי אבא is the husband who brings the complaint. רב שמואל בר אבא is the son who received the property.
steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל's rule is the standard against which רבי ירמיה's ruling is now measured.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba went and said the matter
before Rav Hoshaya;
Rav Hoshaya went and said it
before Rav Yehuda.
He said to him: This is what Shmuel said:
A woman who sold her usufruct property
in her husband's lifetime, and she died —
the husband takes it out of the buyers' hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an earlier authority's ruling that goes against the ruling in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's ruling giving the property to the son.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל rules that a wife's sale of נכסי מלוג fails against the husband after she dies. The son's case should be the same, so the husband should get the property.

steps.title: Rabbi Yirmeya cites a משנה about a father writing property to his son
steps.stepSummary: When told of שמואל's ruling, רבי ירמיה answers that he knows a משנה. It discusses a father who writes his property to his son 'after death' and sets out what each of them can sell.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told it to Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba. He said: I know a משנה, as we learned: One who writes his property to his son for after his death — the son cannot sell, because it is in the father's possession; and the father cannot sell, because it is written to the son. If the father sold, it is sold until he dies. If the son sold, the buyer has nothing until the father dies.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה defends his ruling by quoting a משנה. This step only lays out the משנה; the next step draws the proof from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, ownership is split. The son owns the property itself, while the father keeps its use for life. A father's sale lasts only while he is alive. A son's sale is real, but the buyer must wait until the father dies to take the property.

phrases.aramaic: אַמְרוּהָ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: They said it before Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba;
phrases.notes: They told him שמואל's ruling, which seems to go against what he had decided.

phrases.english: he said to them: I know a Mishnah,

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: הַכּוֹתֵב נְכָסָיו לִבְנוֹ לְאַחַר מוֹתוֹ –
phrases.english: as we learned: One who writes his property to his son for after his death —
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in בבא בתרא 136a.

phrases.english: the son cannot sell,
because they are in the father's possession;
and the father cannot sell,
because they are written to the son.
If the father sold — they are sold until he dies.

phrases.aramaic: מָכַר הַבֵּן – אֵין לוֹ לַלּוֹקֵחַ עַד שֶׁיָּמוּת הָאָב.
phrases.english: If the son sold — the buyer has nothing until the father dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers שמואל's ruling by bringing a משנה that supports the original ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ירמיה's ruling that the son keeps the property.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in בבא בתרא about a father who writes his property to his son for after his death.

steps.title: The son's sale holds even if the son died first
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה reads the משנה closely. Once the father dies, the buyer gets the property, even if the son who sold it died before the father and never held it.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, when the father dies the buyer has it — even though the son died in the father's lifetime, so the property never came into the son's hands.
steps.whatsHappening: Here רבי ירמיה draws the actual proof from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say the buyer loses if the son dies first. It simply says the buyer gets the property when the father dies. So a sale by the one who owns the property itself holds, even if the seller dies before the other person's rights end. In the same way, the mother's transfer to her son holds.

phrases.english: In any event, when the father dies
the buyer has it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּמֵת הַבֵּן בְּחַיֵּי אָב –
phrases.english: and even though the son died in the father's lifetime —
so that they never came into the son's hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי מָיֵית אָב מִיהָא אִית לֵיהּ לְלוֹקֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That a sale by the owner of the property itself holds even if the seller dies first.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The plain wording of the משנה: 'the buyer has nothing until the father dies,' which implies the buyer does get it once the father dies, with no exception for the son dying first.

steps.title: This reading follows ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי ירמיה's reading of the משנה matches ריש לקיש. He holds that the buyer acquires whether the son died first or the father died first.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like רבי שמעון בן לקיש, who said: It makes no difference whether the son died in the father's lifetime, so the property never reached the son, or the father died in the son's lifetime, so it did reach the son — the buyer acquired.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says whose opinion רבי ירמיה's reasoning depends on: רבי שמעון בן לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש says the son's sale works in both cases. The order of the deaths does not matter, and the buyer acquires either way. By linking the proof to his opinion, the גמרא shows the proof works only if ריש לקיש's reading of the משנה is accepted.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ירמיה supports giving the property to the son with the משנה of 'one who writes his property to his son.' He reads it like ריש לקיש: the son's sale holds whether he dies before or after his father. שמואל, though, rules that the husband takes back נכסי מלוג his wife sold.
steps.whyThisMatters: Naming ריש לקיש as the source shows that this proof depends on how one reads the משנה.

phrases.english: Like Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, who said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא מֵת הַבֵּן בְּחַיֵּי הָאָב –
phrases.english: It makes no difference if the son died in the father's lifetime —
where they never came into the son's hands,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא מֵת הָאָב בְּחַיֵּי הַבֵּן –
phrases.english: or if the father died in the son's lifetime —
where they came into the son's hands;
the buyer acquired.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the אמורא whose view the inference in step 4 follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to ריש לקיש, a son's sale of property written to him by his father holds whether the son or the father dies first.

steps.title: The dispute: the son sold and then died before his father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the dispute. If the son sold and then died during the father's lifetime, רבי יוחנן says the buyer did not acquire, and ריש לקיש says the buyer did acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: If the son sold the property during the father's lifetime, and the son died during the father's lifetime, רבי יוחנן says the buyer did not acquire it. ריש לקיש says the buyer did acquire it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the actual dispute it just mentioned. This shows where ריש לקיש's view, the one that matches רבי ירמיה, comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is narrow: the son sold, and then the son died first, so he never held the property himself. רבי יוחנן says the sale is empty. ריש לקיש says that when the father dies, the buyer takes the property.
steps.confusionAlert: Both agree the buyer cannot use the property while the father is alive. They argue only about what happens after the father dies, when the son died first.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute is the backing for רבי ירמיה's ruling in favor of רב שמואל בר אבא, against שמואל's rule quoted by רב יהודה.

phrases.english: As it was stated: If the son sold during the father's lifetime,
and the son died during the father's lifetime –

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לֹא קָנָה לוֹקֵחַ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: The buyer did not acquire,
Reish Lakish says: The buyer acquired.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִתְּמַר: מָכַר הַבֵּן בְּחַיֵּי הָאָב, וּמֵת הַבֵּן בְּחַיֵּי הָאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the full source of the ריש לקיש view mentioned in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: the buyer did not acquire. ריש לקיש: the buyer acquired.

steps.title: How רבי יוחנן reads the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the משנה gives the buyer the property only when the son outlived the father and the property reached the son. If the son died first, the buyer gets nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן, who says the buyer did not acquire, would tell you: When the משנה teaches 'the son sold, the buyer does not acquire until the father dies,' which implies the buyer gets it once the father dies, it is talking about a son who did not die in the father's lifetime, so the property came into the son's hands. But if the son died in the father's lifetime, so the property never came into his hands, then even when the father dies the buyer gets nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי יוחנן deals with the משנה that seemed to support the buyer. He limits it to a son who outlived his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה implies that the buyer gets the property after the father dies. רבי יוחנן says this is true only if the property passed into the son's hands first. If the son died before the father, the property never reached him, so nothing passes to the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you (how this view would answer)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר לֹא קָנָה לוֹקֵחַ –
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan, who says the buyer did not acquire –
would say to you: When our Mishnah teaches

phrases.aramaic: ״מָכַר הַבֵּן – לֹא קָנָה לוֹקֵחַ עַד שֶׁיָּמוּת הָאָב״,
phrases.english: 'If the son sold, the buyer does not acquire until the father dies,'

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָיֵית הָאָב אִית לֵיהּ לְלוֹקֵחַ –
phrases.english: and when the father dies the buyer has it –
that is where the son did not die in the father's lifetime,
so it came into the son's hands.
But if the son died in the father's lifetime,
so it never came into the son's hands –

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מָיֵית אָב נָמֵי לֵית לֵיהּ לְלוֹקֵחַ.
phrases.english: then even when the father dies, the buyer does not have it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר לֹא קָנָה לוֹקֵחַ – אָמַר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי יוחנן's side of the dispute quoted in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's buyer gets the property only if the son outlived the father and the property reached the son.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reason: owning the produce is like owning the item
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws out רבי יוחנן's underlying view. Owning the produce counts like owning the item itself, so the son sold what was not his.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it turns out that he holds that owning the produce is like owning the item itself. When the son sold, he sold something that was not his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls out the principle behind רבי יוחנן's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father kept the produce for his lifetime. רבי יוחנן treats that as if the father still owned the field itself. So at the time of the sale the son owned nothing he could sell. If he dies before the father, there is nothing to pass on to the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: It turns out / so we see
Ownership of the produce (the right to use and eat from it)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: קנין פירות כקנין הגוף דמי. The father's right to the produce makes the son's sale a sale of something not his.
steps.whyThisMatters: This same idea fits a husband's rights to his wife's נכסי מלוג from step 2. If his produce rights count as ownership, the wife's sale does not hold against him.

phrases.english: So it turns out he holds:
ownership of the produce is like ownership of the item itself,
and when he sold, he sold what was not his.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the reason behind רבי יוחנן's reading in step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן holds that קנין פירות is like קנין הגוף, so the son's sale was of something not his.

steps.title: How ריש לקיש reads the משנה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reads the משנה as giving the buyer the property whenever the father dies. It makes no difference whether the son outlived the father or died first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש says the buyer acquired. When the משנה teaches 'the son sold, the buyer has nothing until the father dies,' it means that at least once the father dies, the buyer has it. It makes no difference if the son did not die in the father's lifetime, so the property came into his hands. And it makes no difference if the son died in the father's lifetime, so it never came into his hands. Either way the buyer acquired.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains ריש לקיש's side. He reads the same line of the משנה with no limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, the only thing the buyer waits for is the father's death. Whether the property ever reached the son does not matter. This is the reading רבי ירמיה used in step 4.
steps.whatToRemember: Both read the same משנה. רבי יוחנן limits it to a son who outlived the father. ריש לקיש says the buyer acquires in both cases.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אוֹמֵר קָנָה לוֹקֵחַ –
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, who says the buyer acquired –
When our Mishnah teaches:

phrases.aramaic: ״מָכַר הַבֵּן אֵין לַלּוֹקֵחַ עַד שֶׁיָּמוּת הָאָב״ –
phrases.english: 'If the son sold, the buyer has nothing until the father dies' –

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מָיֵית אָב מִיהַת אִית לֵיהּ לְלוֹקֵחַ;
phrases.english: at least when the father dies, the buyer has it;

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא לָא מֵת הַבֵּן בְּחַיֵּי הָאָב –
phrases.english: no difference whether the son did not die in the father's lifetime –
so it came into the son's hands,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא שְׁנָא מֵת הַבֵּן בְּחַיֵּי הָאָב –
phrases.english: or whether the son died in the father's lifetime –
so it never came into the son's hands;
the buyer acquired.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אוֹמֵר קָנָה לוֹקֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reading of the same משנה line that רבי יוחנן limited in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the father dies, the buyer acquires, whether or not the son outlived the father.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's underlying view: owning the produce is not owning the item
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws out the reasoning behind ריש לקיש. Owning the produce is not like owning the item itself, so the son sold property that was really his.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems ריש לקיש holds that owning the produce is not like owning the item itself. When the son sold, he sold what belonged to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why ריש לקיש lets the buyer keep the property even if the son died first. In his view, the father's right to the produce never took ownership away from the son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches step 8, which explained רבי יוחנן, but it reaches the opposite conclusion. רבי יוחנן said the father's produce rights count as owning the field, so the son had nothing to sell. ריש לקיש says the father only holds the produce, so the son owned the field itself and his sale was valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Owning only the produce or profits of an item

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says owning the produce is like owning the item, so the son's sale fails. ריש לקיש says it is not, so the son's sale works.

phrases.english: Apparently, he holds:
phrases.notes: "He" is ריש לקיש, whose view was just quoted in step 9.

phrases.aramaic: קִנְיַן פֵּירוֹת לָאו כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: ownership of the produce is not like ownership of the item itself,
and when he sold, he sold what was his.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the small word קא in the round brackets. The meaning stays the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the reason behind ריש לקיש's reading of the משנה in step 9, matching what step 8 did for רבי יוחנן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ריש לקיש holds that קנין פירות is not like קנין הגוף, so the son owned the field and could sell it.

steps.title: Both רבי ירמיה בר אבא and רב יהודה follow ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the earlier argument and states that both רבי ירמיה בר אבא and רב יהודה hold like ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, both רבי ירמיה בר אבא and רב יהודה hold like רבי שמעון בן לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the earlier argument between רבי ירמיה בר אבא and רב יהודה. It states that both of them agree with ריש לקיש, and this sets up רבי ירמיה בר אבא's argument in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both sides accept ריש לקיש's view that קנין פירות is not like קנין הגוף, they have a shared starting point. This is why רבי ירמיה בר אבא can use that idea as an argument against רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: And now, as for us (returning to our topic)
Whether... or (both one and the other)

phrases.english: And now, as for us,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא וּבֵין רַב יְהוּדָה –
phrases.english: both Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba and Rav Yehuda

phrases.aramaic: כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ סְבִירָא לְהוּ.
phrases.english: hold like Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish.
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון בן לקיש is the full name of ריש לקיש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש dispute and returns to רבי ירמיה בר אבא and רב יהודה, placing both on ריש לקיש's side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both רבי ירמיה בר אבא and רב יהודה hold that קנין פירות is not like קנין הגוף.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה בר אבא proves the point from the case where the son died first
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא argues that if owning the produce were like owning the item, the buyer would get nothing when the son died before the father. The משנה gives the buyer the property, so that cannot be the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא says: if owning the produce were like owning the item itself, then why does the buyer get the property when the father dies after the son already died? The son would have sold something that was not his!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה בר אבא brings a proof from the משנה, read the way ריש לקיש reads it. He shows that the opposite idea leads to a result the משנה does not allow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Following ריש לקיש, the משנה gives the buyer the property even when the son died first. If the father's produce rights made him the owner, the son would have sold what was not his, and the buyer should get nothing. Since the buyer does get the property, the father's produce rights must not count as ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind (if you were to think)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba says:
If it enters your mind
that owning the produce is like owning the item itself,
then when the father dies
and the son had died in the father's lifetime,
why does the buyer get it?
When this one (the son) sold,
he sold what was not his!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָאָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the shared ריש לקיש starting point from step 11 to build a proof from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That קנין פירות is not like קנין הגוף.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה, read like ריש לקיש, which gives the buyer the property even when the son died during the father's lifetime.

steps.title: The proof's conclusion: owning the produce is not owning the item
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא concludes his proof: we must learn from the משנה that owning the produce is not like owning the item itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: So isn't it clear from here that owning the produce is not like owning the item itself?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה בר אבא finishes his argument and states the lesson he draws from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 showed that the opposite idea does not fit the משנה. Here he states the conclusion: קנין פירות is not like קנין הגוף. He uses this against רב יהודה's ruling, which seemed to treat the husband's produce rights as stronger than the wife's ownership.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (we can conclude from here)

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it so? Learn from it

phrases.aramaic: קִנְיַן פֵּירוֹת לָאו כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: that owning the produce is not like owning the item itself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the conclusion of the proof built in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי ירמיה בר אבא, the משנה shows that קנין פירות is not like קנין הגוף.

steps.title: רב יהודה answers in the name of שמואל: this case is not like our משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא's argument is brought back to רב יהודה. He answers that שמואל said this case is not similar to our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought the argument back to רב יהודה. He told them: this is what שמואל said, "This case is not similar to our משנה."
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה pushes back against the proof. He quotes שמואל, who said the משנה cannot be used for the case they were discussing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה does not deny what the משנה says about the father and son. Instead, he says the משנה's case and שמואל's ruling about the wife are different situations, so a proof from one does not carry over to the other. The next steps explain what the difference is.

keyTerms.meaning: They brought it back (returned the argument)

steps.confusionAlert: רב יהודה is not arguing with the rule that קנין פירות is not like קנין הגוף. He only says the משנה's case does not apply to his ruling.

phrases.english: They brought it back before Rav Yehuda;
he said to them: This is what Shmuel said:
This is not similar to our Mishnah.
phrases.notes: "This" is שמואל's ruling that רב יהודה quoted in step 2: a husband takes back property his wife sold before she died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the proof from steps 12 and 13 by saying the משנה's case cannot be compared to רב יהודה's ruling.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the משנה as proof against רב יהודה's ruling, without rejecting what the משנה itself teaches.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof compares two cases that שמואל says are not similar.

steps.title: Why is the woman's case different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind שמואל's statement that the woman's case is not like our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why שמואל said the woman's case does not match the משנה. This short question sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14, שמואל only said the cases are different without explaining why. Now the גמרא wants to know what the actual difference is.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why did שמואל say the woman's case isn't like our משנה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind שמואל's distinction quoted in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes the woman's case different from the משנה of one who writes his property to his son.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the son can sell because he is fit to inherit
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the משנה cannot prove that owning the produce is unlike owning the item. It speaks about a son, and a son is fit to inherit anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: If the משנה had taught the opposite case, a man who writes his property to his father, we could prove from it that owning the produce is not like owning the item. But the משנה speaks about a man who writes his property to his son. The son's sale works because he is fit to inherit his father.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains שמואל. The משנה's ruling about the son is special, because a son is the natural heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה בר אבא used the משנה to prove that owning the produce is not like owning the item. רב יוסף says the son's sale may work for a different reason: he is the expected heir and already has a strong tie to the property. The woman's case has no such heir relationship, so the משנה does not help there.

keyTerms.meaning: ownership of the produce (the right to use and profit)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said,
Granted, if it had taught the opposite:
"One who writes his property to his father" –
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא imagines the משנה the other way around: a son giving to his father instead of a father giving to his son.

phrases.english: it would be possible to prove from it

phrases.aramaic: דְּקִנְיַן פֵּירוֹת לָאו כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: that owning the produce is not like owning the item itself.
But now that it teaches:
"One who writes his property to his son,"
it is because he is fit to inherit him.
phrases.notes: So the son's sale works because he is the heir, not because of the produce-ownership rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, בִּשְׁלָמָא אִי תָּנֵי אִיפְּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 by explaining שמואל's distinction.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה's case is a son, the natural heir. His right to sell comes from that, so no general rule about owning the produce can be proven from it.

steps.title: אביי: a father inherits a son just as a son inherits a father
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב יוסף. Inheritance goes both ways, and the משנה used a son only because that case explains why someone would write his property to another person.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Does a son inherit a father, but a father does not inherit a son?! Rather, in the reverse case, the son would be writing to his father to keep the property away from his own son. Here too, the father writes to one son to keep the property away from that son's brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's reason. A father is also an heir, so being an heir cannot be what makes the son special.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said a son is special because he is fit to inherit. אביי answers that a father inherits from his son too, so the reverse case would also have an heir. The משנה picked a son only because it is a normal situation: a father wants one son to get everything instead of the brothers. So the משנה's wording proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say...? (a challenging question)
to move them away, to keep property away from someone

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Is that to say that a son inherits a father,
but a father does not inherit a son?!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְאַבְרוֹחִינְהוּ לְנִכְסֵי מִבְּרֵיהּ קָא אָתֵי;
phrases.english: Rather, he comes to keep the property away from his son;
phrases.notes: In the reverse case, the son writes to his father so that his own son won't inherit.

phrases.english: here too,
he comes to keep the property away from his brothers.
phrases.notes: In the משנה's case, the father picks one son so the other sons won't share.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אַטּוּ בְּרָא יָרֵית אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's explanation in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the son's sale works because a son is fit to inherit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inheritance goes both ways, so a father would also be fit to inherit. The משנה chose a son only because a father commonly wants to keep property from the other brothers.

steps.title: אביי's own reason: the תקנת אושא
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that שמואל's distinction rests on the rabbinic rule made in אושא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does "it is not like our משנה" mean? It is because of the תקנת אושא.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting רב יוסף, אביי gives his own explanation of שמואל. The woman's case is different because of a special rule the חכמים made in אושא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference has nothing to do with heirs. In the woman's case, a rabbinic rule gives the husband extra rights over her property. No such rule exists for a father and son, so the משנה's ruling still stands in its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not similar to our משנה
the rabbinic rule made in the town of אושא

phrases.english: Rather, what is "it is not similar to our משנה"?
phrases.notes: This quotes שמואל's words from step 14.

phrases.english: Because of the ordinance of Usha.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's rejected explanation with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The woman's case is different because of the special rabbinic rule from אושא about a husband and his wife's property.
steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל's statement is no longer a challenge to the rule that owning the produce is not like owning the item. The woman's case is simply governed by a special rabbinic rule.

steps.title: The תקנת אושא about a wife's נכסי מלוג
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא reports the rule of אושא: if a wife sold her נכסי מלוג while her husband was alive and then died, the husband takes the property back from the buyers.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: In אושא they made a rule. If a woman sold her נכסי מלוג while her husband was alive and then she died, the husband takes the property back from the buyers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the rule of אושא to show what אביי means. It explains why the husband wins in the woman's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a sale by the owner of the item itself would stand. The חכמים in אושא gave the husband a special right to take back his wife's נכסי מלוג from buyers after she dies. This special rule is the real reason for the husband's win, not a general rule about owning the produce.

keyTerms.meaning: a wife's property: she owns it, the husband eats its produce
takes it back from the buyers

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's case is different only because of the תקנת אושא, a special rule for husbands. The proof that owning the produce is not like owning the item itself still stands.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the תקנת אושא shows that owning the produce is like owning the item. It is a special rabbinic rule for a husband, made on top of the basic law.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:
In Usha they instituted,
a woman who sold her usufruct property
in her husband's lifetime, and died –
the husband takes it back from the buyers.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא: בְּאוּשָׁא הִתְקִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source and content of the תקנת אושא mentioned in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that the woman's case is governed by the תקנת אושא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי בר חנינא's report of the rule made in אושא about a wife's נכסי מלוג.

steps.title: רב אידי בר אבין begins bringing support from witnesses about a divorce
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין says that a known teaching already supports the rule of אושא. He starts quoting it: witnesses say a man divorced his wife and paid her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין said: We have also learned this rule in a teaching: "We testify that a certain man divorced his wife and paid her כתובה..."
steps.whatsHappening: רב אידי בר אבין starts bringing a proof for the rule of אושא from an earlier teaching. This line only sets up the case, and the point of the proof comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase אף אנן נמי תנינא means a teaching already says what we just heard. So רב אידי בר אבין is claiming that the rule of אושא, which gives the husband rights in his wife's property, can be seen in an older source. Here we only get the start of the case, witnesses testifying about a divorce and a כתובה payment. How it proves the rule comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned this, meaning an existing teaching supports what was just said
We testify, the opening words of witnesses in court
The marriage contract, which promises the wife money if she is divorced or widowed

steps.confusionAlert: The quote is not finished here. Don't try to see the proof yet, because it only becomes clear once the rest of the case is quoted in the next lines.

phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin said:
We too have learned this:
phrases.notes: "This" is the rule of אושא from the last step. He is about to quote a teaching that shows it.

phrases.english: "We testify about a certain man
that he divorced his wife,
and paid her marriage contract,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an existing teaching to support the rule of אושא reported in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: The rule of אושא, which gives the husband a claim on his wife's נכסי מלוג that is stronger than a buyer's
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching about witnesses who testify that a man divorced his wife and paid her כתובה (the quote continues in the next lines)
